claims.text: The as-cast HfMoTaTiZr baseline has a homogeneous single-phase BCC structure.
The as-cast HfMoTaTiZr baseline has a density of approximately 10.21 g/cm³.
The as-cast HfMoTaTiZr baseline has a room-temperature yield strength of approximately 1600 MPa.
The as-cast HfMoTaTiZr baseline has a yield strength of approximately 855 MPa at 1000°C.
The proposed intervention replaces approximately 20% of the Mo sublattice with V to form HfMo0.8V0.2TaTiZr.
HfMo0.8V0.2TaTiZr will retain a homogeneous single-phase BCC solid solution.
Substitutional V will increase lattice distortion because of atomic-size mismatch with the other alloying elements.
Mo has a density of approximately 10.2 g/cm³.
V has a density of approximately 6.0 g/cm³.
Replacing part of the Mo content with lighter V will lower the alloy density.
Increased chemical disorder and lattice strain from V substitution will enhance solid-solution strengthening.
Appropriate calibration of V content can preserve the single-phase microstructure and avoid deleterious secondary phases.
At y approximately 0.2, V substitution will reduce density by approximately 10% relative to the HfMoTaTiZr baseline.
At y approximately 0.2, the modified alloy will retain a room-temperature yield strength near or above 1600 MPa.
At y approximately 0.2, the modified alloy will have a yield strength around or above 850 MPa at 1000°C.
The modified alloy will have fracture toughness similar to or slightly better than the baseline.
The precise solubility limit of V in the HfMoTaTiZr matrix is uncertain.
V substitution may produce secondary phases if the substitution level is not optimally controlled.
The proposed mechanical comparison is limited to quasi-static loading at room temperature and 1000°C.

contradictions.description: The boundary says testing is confined to quasi-static tensile loading, whereas the conditions and experimental design also require standardized fracture-toughness loading.
